turns.q: Honestly, is the pricier one worth the extra, or is the cheaper one fine?
turns.replyTail:
AI Assistant
Here to help you shop
menu
The extra cost for Low Tide ($6.69 / sq ft) comes down purely to aesthetics: you get wider 8" planks (compared to ~6" on High Five) and a brushed wood texture rather than a smooth finish, which creates a more expansive, textured look.
If you want to stretch your budget as far as possible, High Five is all you need. However, if wider planks and a brushed texture fit your design vision better, the small upgrade to Low Tide can be well worth it.
